assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines the physiology of proglucagon-derived GLP-1 as an incretin and carries it through to therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. The link from basic hormone biology to broad clinical and public-health impact is exceptionally clear, and the discovery is original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion/action in humans) and Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, intestinotrophic and cardiometabolic actions) are core basic contributors; Knudsen carried the molecule through to a durable, long-acting drug. Mojsov's early peptide characterization is a real contribution whose weight relative to others is contested, and other figures outside the supplied credit may also matter. The three-person configuration is defensible but not uncontested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of mechanistic work, multiple independent large outcome trials, and wide approval of semaglutide- and liraglutide-class drugs. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Mojsov, Holst, Drucker and others (including people not on the supplied list) is unresolved.
Whether the prize should honour physiology, drug development, or both; I have not verified all priority claims independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with synthetic receptors to eliminate cancer is a conceptually new therapeutic modality, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and spillover into autoimmunity and next-generation cell engineering.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation, costimulatory design in the clinic) and Sadelain (CD28-costimulated second-generation CAR, preclinical proof of concept) are the central named figures. Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work is foundational for the field but is a distinct line, and the original chimeric-receptor concept predates all three; the supplied credit may not capture all founders.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and over a decade of follow-up demonstrating durable responses. Limits in solid tumors and toxicity remain but do not undermine the core discovery. Timely.
uncertainties: The original chimeric antigen receptor concept came from others who are not in the supplied credit, so a fair three-person prize is hard to define.
Long-term safety signals (secondary malignancies) are still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean mechanism-to-medicine chain: dissecting SMN2 exon 7 splicing, designing an antisense oligonucleotide to correct it, and thereby converting a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one (nusinersen). It established splice-modulating oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) form a natural pair. Contributions of clinical investigators and the original SMN gene discovery lie outside the supplied credit, so the configuration is narrow but coherent.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with robust long-term outcome data; the paradigm has been extended to other ASO therapies. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Relative weighting against the SMN gene discovery and other SMA therapies (gene therapy, small-molecule splicing modifiers) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus (Ire1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing) that senses protein-folding load. It revealed an entirely new class of organelle-to-nucleus communication and is now central to understanding of secretory, metabolic, neurodegenerative and malignant disease.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily defined the pathway's core components and mechanism; the pairing is compact and widely seen as appropriate. Others in the field contributed later branches (PERK, ATF6) but the original signaling logic is credited to these two.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of independent confirmation and conserved mechanism from yeast to mammals. Clinical translation is still emerging, but the basic discovery stands on its own.
uncertainties: The strength of direct therapeutic consequences is still developing; the case rests mainly on fundamental biology.
How to treat contributions on the PERK and ATF6 arms in a prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsins and related tools allow millisecond-scale control of genetically defined cells, which reshaped causal neuroscience across circuits, behavior and disease models. It is a methodological invention with very broad lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth (with Boyden) delivered it to neurons and developed the toolkit; Miesenböck made an earlier distinct demonstration of genetically targeted photostimulation. Six credited names for at most three places makes fair allocation the main difficulty, and any choice leaves out strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the research domain, with thousands of independent applications. Clinical translation (retinal optogenetic therapy) is early.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the molecular discoverers (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the neuronal-application pioneers (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenböck) is unresolved.
It is a tool rather than a disease mechanism, which may weigh differently under the prize's criteria.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-lived, self-organizing three-dimensional cultures from single adult Lgr5-positive stem cells created a general platform for modeling tissue biology, infection, cancer and personalized drug testing. Original and broadly enabling, grounded in the discovery of intestinal stem cell markers.
assessment.attribution: Clevers (Lgr5 stem cell identity and the organoid concept) is the clear intellectual driver; Sato was first author on the founding culture work. Other organoid lineages (pluripotent-derived, e.g. Sasai, Lancaster) are outside this credit and complicate a general 'organoid' citation.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent adoption and growing translational use, though clinical impact is still emerging.
uncertainties: Whether a fair prize would need to include pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work not in the supplied credit.
Clinical and regulatory impact is still limited relative to the research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib for BCR-ABL-driven chronic myeloid leukemia proved that inhibiting a defining oncogenic kinase can turn a fatal cancer into a manageable chronic condition, and it launched modern targeted oncology. The impact is large and clearly demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio. The BCR-ABL fusion discovery and chemistry teams, whose work was earlier, fall outside this credit, and some would argue the oncogene story is the more fundamental discovery.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with more than twenty years of survival data and many successor kinase inhibitors. Recognition is somewhat late rather than premature, but other candidates seem more discovery-driven.
uncertainties: Fit with a prize for discovery versus drug development, and omission of earlier BCR-ABL fusion work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central controller of cell growth in response to nutrients links a fundamental signaling hub to aging, cancer, immunosuppression and metabolism. Original, widely confirmed and conceptually unifying.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered the TOR genes and their function; Schreiber's chemical-genetic work identified the FKBP12-rapamycin target relationship. Sabatini's mTORC1 nutrient-sensing contributions are significant, but I would not include him here given unresolved questions about the strength of the supplied credit; this reflects judgment rather than verified fact. Other contributors to the original rapamycin and TOR discovery (e.g. Heitman, Movva, Hall's group members, Sabatini's predecessors) are outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with strong independent confirmation. Therapeutic exploitation (rapalogs, mTOR inhibitors) is established though modest in some indications.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini is unresolved, and the roles of other early investigators are not captured.
I have not independently verified all priority claims.
